episode.title: Cariboo Signals - Repair Culture & Practical Tech
episode.description:
Riley and Casey explore technology and society in rural communities. Today's focus: Repair Culture & Practical Tech.

THIS WEEK WE'RE ASKING: Why is everyone in tech so sad?

NEWS ROUNDUP: We break down [Williams Lake Tribune] Bewitching Market coming up in Williams Lake following steampunk themed bazaar and A beauty night in store August 19th at the Williams Lake Stampede Grounds : My Cariboo Now, plus 1 more stories, and explore what these developments mean for communities like ours.

RURAL CONNECTIONS: Does repair work—physical or digital—carry inherent meaning that building new things lacks, and can recognizing maintenance as valuable as new launches address burnout in tech? Topics include: Retrofit architecture versus new construction economics and emissions, AI-generated code security risks and repair literacy gaps, Why maintenance work in tech goes invisible and uncredited, How visibility and accountability for long-term maintenance affects worker meaning, Structural incentive design in industries that reward staying versus leaving.

Hosts: Riley (Tech optimist with an engineering background) and Casey (Community-first skeptic of tech promises).

COMMUNITY SPOTLIGHT: New Focus Society

articles.title: Summerland wildlife rehab centre vows to rebuild after losing everything to wildfire : My Cariboo Now

discussion.central_question: Does repair work—physical or digital—carry inherent meaning that building new things lacks, and can recognizing maintenance as valuable as new launches address burnout in tech?
discussion.riley_position: Repair work carries psychological and moral weight because it produces a visible, tangible outcome you can point to afterward, and tech could address its burnout crisis by formally crediting maintenance and repair work the same way it credits new launches.
riley_key_evidence: Ken Soble Tower retrofit produces 50-75% less embodied carbon than new construction
Summerland wildlife rehab centre operators are rebuilding with visible, purposeful work ahead of them
School District 27 and Xatśūll's approaches show communities can design systems for long-term maintenance from day one
discussion.casey_position: The real problem is structural incentive misalignment rather than physical versus abstract work; tech rewards new launches and walks away from maintenance, while invisible legacy-system maintenance work already exists but goes uncredited and unfunded.
casey_key_evidence: 2025 survey documents bugs in AI-generated code; USENIX study shows package hallucination attacks where bad actors register fake library names the AI invented
Software repair literacy gap means users can't verify what code is actually running in apps they 'built' with AI in an afternoon
Performance reviews never score 'kept the lights on for three years' as highly as shipping a new product
discussion.resolution: They converge on the structural diagnosis: the issue isn't repair versus new-build work itself, but that tech industry design rewards walking away after launch and leaving maintenance to whoever remains. They agree to test whether publicly naming maintainers—without knowing if visibility alone can close the deeper despair—is worth trying as a Cariboo experiment.
